solutionSql:
SELECT s.customer_id,
       COUNT(i.id)::int AS billed_invoices,
       (DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(i.id) DESC))::int AS billed_rank
FROM shipments AS s
JOIN invoices AS i ON i.shipment_id = s.id
GROUP BY s.customer_id
ORDER BY billed_rank, s.customer_id;

ambiguities.phrase: the number of invoices on their shipments
ambiguities.readingChosen: Count invoice rows joined to the customer shipments (inner join, so customers whose shipments have no invoice drop out).
ambiguities.alternativeReading: Count distinct shipments that have an invoice; identical here because each shipment has at most one invoice.

notes: Inner join shipments to invoices, group by customer_id, DENSE_RANK over the count descending for gapless shared ranks. COUNT and DENSE_RANK return bigint, so both are cast to integer to match the expected column types. Customers with no invoice are excluded by the inner join.
